C-001.statement: SGD does not reach the skull when only the NEAT links of the raw architecture can learn.
C-001.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10].
C-001.prediction: At most 1 of 3 G1a seeds on skull reaches MSE < 0.01, replicating FER paper Fig. 12.
C-001.flip_boundary: Unknown; the fit threshold is looser than dense SGD (about 5e-4), so a pass here is a weak fit.

C-002.statement: Weights that SGD finds on Picbreeder wiring do not reproduce the symmetry Picbreeder weights achieve on neurons whose parity the wiring leaves free.
C-002.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. Wiring facts known before registration: the Picbreeder masks force the parity of 82%/59%/38% of distinct maps (skull/butterfly/apple), for any weights. Skull is excluded: its Picbreeder network has only 3 free maps.
C-002.prediction: For M1x, r = (G1b - PB) / (G0 - PB) is at least 0.7 on butterfly and apple. r <= 0.3 falsifies: the wiring would then be sufficient. Between them is MIXED.
C-002.flip_boundary: Low redundancy on a sparse network may push SGD toward reuse, which would lower r.

C-003.statement: Most of the Picbreeder-vs-dense gap in perturbation asymmetry comes from the wiring, not from how the weights were found.
C-003.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. Wiring facts known before registration: the Picbreeder masks force the parity of 82%/59%/38% of distinct maps (skull/butterfly/apple), for any weights.
C-003.prediction: For M3a and M4a, r = (G1b - PB) / (G0 - PB) is at most 0.3 on all three tasks. r >= 0.7 falsifies. Between them is MIXED.
C-003.flip_boundary: Weaker where the mask forces less parity, so apple is the most likely to break this.

C-004.statement: Sparsity alone does not close the gap: pruning a dense SGD network to the same edge count per layer leaves its symmetry metrics near those of the dense network.
C-004.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. G4 keeps the Picbreeder edge count in each layer, but SGD chooses the edges by magnitude. M1x excludes skull, whose Picbreeder network has only 3 free maps.
C-004.prediction: For M1, M3a and M4a on all tasks, and M1x on butterfly and apple, r = (G4 - PB) / (G0 - PB) is at least 0.7. r <= 0.3 on any falsifies: sparsity would then explain that gap. Between them is MIXED.
C-004.flip_boundary: Pruning may keep near-symmetric edges if the near-symmetric target rewards them.
C-004.withdrawn_reason: Design error found in a dry run before any G4 data: Picbreeder's per-layer edge counts go as low as 1 on skull, so magnitude pruning to those counts would sever output channels and make a fit failure an artifact. Replaced by C-005.

C-005.statement: Sparsity alone does not close the gap: pruning a dense SGD network to the same total edge count leaves its symmetry metrics near those of the dense network.
C-005.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. G4 keeps the Picbreeder total edge count, spread evenly over hidden layers with one edge per output channel, chosen over five rounds by path strength from the dense SGD network, then fine-tuned. M1x excludes skull, whose Picbreeder network has only 3 free maps.
C-005.flip_boundary: Pruning may keep near-symmetric edges if the near-symmetric target rewards them.
C-005.prediction: For M1, M3a and M4a on all tasks, and M1x on butterfly and apple, r = (G4 - PB) / (G0 - PB) is at least 0.7. r <= 0.3 on any falsifies: sparsity would then explain that gap. Between them is MIXED.

C-006.statement: Fit level alone does not make a network Picbreeder-like: a dense network stopped at the fit level of the pruned networks keeps symmetry metrics near those of the fully trained dense network.
C-006.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. G0e is the dense architecture and seeds of G0, stopped the first time its full-image MSE is at most 0.0065, about the median MSE of fitted G4 runs on butterfly (0.0067) and apple (0.0066). Written after seeing the G4 results, as a check on how to read C-005; skull has no fitted G4 run to match.
C-006.flip_boundary: Early training may favour low-frequency symmetric features on near-symmetric targets, which would lower r most on apple.
C-006.prediction: For M1, M1x, M3a and M4a on butterfly and apple, r = (G0e - PB) / (G0 - PB) is at least 0.7. If r <= 0.3, fit level can explain that gap, and the C-005 falsification on apple does not show a sparsity effect.

C-007.statement: Whether the gap survives at a coarse fit depends on the task: on apple dense networks at MSE 0.0065 already score like Picbreeder on M3a and M4a; on butterfly they stay near the fully trained network.
C-007.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. G0e against PB and G0. Apple M1 and M1x are not covered: they were in the middle band.
C-007.flip_boundary: Unknown; only two tasks and one fit level were measured.
C-007.prediction: Post-hoc description of results already seen in C-006, not a prediction. It is kept as a regression lock, and new G0e seeds can still break it.
C-007.note: G0e has a looser adaptation threshold and a higher F than fully fitted groups in phase0/continual.py; this does not affect the M3a and M4a checks here.

C-008.statement: Fixing the copy edges at 1 and training only NEAT links makes butterfly fit reliably.
C-008.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. Batch b6: butterfly seeds 3-8 in each group, fixed in advance; no seeds will be added after seeing results. Only b6 runs count as the test group. A G4 seed whose dense parent misses the fit threshold is not pruned.
C-008.flip_boundary: Skull already failed this setup 3 of 3, so success here would be specific to butterfly.
C-008.prediction: Hypothesis proposed from outside this analysis: at least 4 of 6 G1a seeds reach MSE < 0.01. The analyst expects this to fail, given C-001.

C-009.statement: On butterfly at a similar fit level, Picbreeder wiring with SGD-found weights is closer to Picbreeder than to a dense network, on symmetry metrics.
C-009.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. Batch b6: butterfly seeds 3-8 in each group, fixed in advance; no seeds will be added after seeing results. Only b6 runs count as the test group. A G4 seed whose dense parent misses the fit threshold is not pruned. Reference is G0e, a dense network stopped at MSE <= 0.0065, not the fully trained G0, so that r compares networks at a similar fit level.
C-009.flip_boundary: The wiring forces the parity of 59% of maps, so M1 and M3a are partly fixed by construction; M1x is the part the wiring leaves free.
C-009.prediction: r = (G1b - PB) / (G0e - PB) is at most 0.3 for M1, M1x, M3a and M4a. r >= 0.7 falsifies. Between them is MIXED. This reverses the C-002 prediction, based on one fitted butterfly seed.

C-010.statement: On butterfly at a similar fit level, sparsity alone does not make a network Picbreeder-like: pruned networks stay closer to a dense network.
C-010.scope: 128x128 image regression on the three Picbreeder CPPNs, 50k iterations, Adam with unit-norm gradients, fit = MSE < 0.01. Perturbations act on existing edges only; matched window of mean |dRGB| in [0.02, 0.10]. Batch b6: butterfly seeds 3-8 in each group, fixed in advance; no seeds will be added after seeing results. Only b6 runs count as the test group. A G4 seed whose dense parent misses the fit threshold is not pruned. Reference is G0e, a dense network stopped at MSE <= 0.0065, not the fully trained G0, so that r compares networks at a similar fit level. G4 as in C-005, pruned from b6 dense networks.
C-010.flip_boundary: Results may differ on tasks where coarse fits are already symmetric, as apple is.
C-010.prediction: r = (G4 - PB) / (G0e - PB) is at least 0.7 for M1, M1x, M3a and M4a. r <= 0.3 falsifies. Between them is MIXED.

C-011.statement: Starting from Picbreeder (PBd), a network learns a local symmetric edit with much less disturbance outside the edit than a fully fitted dense network, without being much slower.
C-011.scope: phase0/continual.py: 2000 steps of Adam with unit-norm gradients at each task's training learning rate (lr_scale 1), 64x64. G0 is fully fitted dense SGD, including seeds from batch b6. Three edits per class per task. Rows share networks, so medians are descriptive summaries, not independent samples; Picbreeder is one network per task. lr_scale 0.1 rows are descriptive and count toward no check. PBd starts from Picbreeder with every weight free, so its search space equals G0's. A 30-step smoke test, seen before registration, showed PBd MSE rising at first, because Adam moves all zero weights at once. No full run had been seen. Known biases: Picbreeder weights are larger, so one learning rate is a smaller relative step on existing edges, which can lower interference and slow adaptation; warp targets come from the Picbreeder generator itself.
C-011.flip_boundary: A slower learner moves less per step, so the speed checks guard against reading slowness as low interference.
C-011.prediction: On each task, median F of PBd is at most 0.5 times G0's, and median A1c at most 1.5 times G0's. F ratio >= 1 or A1c ratio >= 3 falsifies. Between them is MIXED. F needs at least 3 adapted runs. Expectation: the smoke test makes the analyst doubt this for PBd.
C-011.note: A1c is right-censored at 2000 steps, so its ratios are lower bounds, not measured ratios. Where both groups are censored, ratio 1.0 and its PASS carry no information. PB is one network per task, and edits on it are not independent samples. The falsification rests on the lower bounds on other tasks and does not change.
